Mesillat Yesharim 7:16: And so you will find that all the deeds of the righteous are always done with haste. Of Abraham it is written (Genesis 18:6): "And Abraham hastened into the tent to Sarah, and said, Hasten, etc."; "and he gave it to the young man, and he hastened."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:17: Rebecca (ibid. 24:20): "And she hastened and emptied her pitcher, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:18: And so they said in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 10): "And the woman hastened, etc." (Judges 13:10) — this teaches that all the deeds of the righteous are done with haste, that they allow no interval of time either at the beginning of a commandment or at its completion.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:19: And you will see that a person whose soul burns with fervor in the service of his Creator will certainly not be lazy in performing his commandments; rather, his motion will be like the swift motion of fire, for he will not rest and will not be still until he has completed the matter and brought it to fulfillment.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:20: And indeed, reflect further, that just as alacrity is the offspring of inner fervor, so from alacrity, in turn, fervor is born. That is, whoever, in performing a commandment, feels himself hastening his outward motion, thereby causes his inner motion to burn likewise, and desire and will grow ever stronger within him. But if he conducts himself sluggishly in the movement of his limbs, the movement of his spirit will also sink and be extinguished. This is a matter to which experience testifies.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:21: And indeed, you already know that what is most desired in the service of the Creator, blessed be His Name, is the desire of the heart and the yearning of the soul. This is what King David glories in as his good portion, saying (Psalms 42:2-3): "As the deer longs for the water brooks, so my soul longs for You, O God; my soul thirsts for God, etc." (Psalms 84:3): "My soul yearns, indeed, it faints, for the courts of the Lord." (Psalms 63:2): "My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:22: However, for a person in whom this longing does not burn as it should, good counsel for him is that he hasten himself willfully, so that from this there will result the birth of longing within him as a matter of nature; for outward motion arouses inward motion, and certainly the outward is more within his own control than the inward. But if he makes use of what is within his power, he will in time acquire also what is not within his power, for inward joy, desire, and longing will be born within him through the fact that he is already hastening his motion willfully. This is what the prophet used to say (Hosea 6:3): "And let us know, let us pursue to know the Lord," and it is written (ibid. 11:10): "They shall walk after the Lord; He shall roar like a lion."
Mesillat Yesharim 8:1:
The Way of Acquiring Alacrity
Now, the means by which alacrity is acquired are the very same as those by which watchfulness is acquired, and their levels are as their levels, as I have written above,
Mesillat Yesharim 8:2: for their matter is very close to one another, and there is no difference between them except that one concerns positive commandments and the other negative commandments.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:3: And when the great value of the commandments and the extent of one's obligation in them become clear to a person, his heart will certainly be aroused to the service, and he will not grow lax in it.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:4: And indeed, what can intensify this arousal is reflecting on the abundance of the good that the Holy One, blessed be He, does for a person at every time and every hour, and the great wonders He performs for him from the moment of his birth until his final day; for the more he looks at and reflects upon these matters, the more he will recognize for himself a great debt to the God who does good to him,
Mesillat Yesharim 8:5: and these will become means for him not to be lazy or lax in his service. For since he certainly cannot repay Him, blessed be He, for His goodness, let him at least give thanks to His Name and fulfill His commandments.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:6: And there is no person, in whatever condition he may find himself — poor or rich, healthy or sick — who will not see great wonders and much good in his own condition.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:7: For the rich and the healthy already owe Him, blessed be He, for their wealth and their health.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:8: The poor man owes Him that even in his poverty He provides his livelihood in a way of miracle and wonder, and does not let him die of hunger.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:9: The sick man owes Him because He sustains him through the severity of his illness and his afflictions, and does not let him go down to the pit — and so on with all similar cases — so that there is no person who will not recognize himself as indebted to his Creator.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:10: And upon reflecting on these good things that he receives from Him, he will certainly be aroused to be alacritous in His service, as I have written above,
Mesillat Yesharim 8:11: all the more so if he reflects that all his good fortune is in His hand, blessed be He, and that whatever he needs and whatever is essential to him comes from Him, blessed be He, and from no other.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:12: Because of this, he will certainly not grow lazy in serving Him, blessed be He, and he will not lack what is essential to him.
Mesillat Yesharim 8:13: And you can see that I have here included, in what I have said, the three levels which I distinguished with regard to watchfulness, for their matter is already one and the same. And the thing is learned from its nature —
Mesillat Yesharim 8:14: namely, that for those complete in understanding, the arousal will come from the side of obligation and from the side of the value and importance of deeds;
Mesillat Yesharim 8:15: for those lesser than they, from the side of the World to Come and its honor, so that shame will not overtake him on the Day of Reward, seeing the good he could have attained and lost;
Mesillat Yesharim 8:16: and for the masses, from the side of this world and its needs, in the manner I explained above.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:1:
An Explanation of the Things That Undermine Alacrity, and How to Distance Oneself from Them
Now, the things that undermine alacrity are the very things that magnify laziness. And the greatest of them all is the pursuit of bodily rest, the hatred of exertion, and the love of comforts, with the fulfillment of all their conditions.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:2: For such a person will certainly find the service before his Creator exceedingly heavy. For whoever wishes to eat his meals in complete comfort and rest, and to sleep his sleep undisturbed, and refuses to walk except at a leisurely pace, and the like — it will be hard for him to rise early for synagogue in the morning, or to cut short his meal for the Mincha prayer in the late afternoon, or to go out for a matter of a commandment unless the time is fully convenient, all the more so to hasten himself for words of a commandment or Torah study.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:3: And whoever accustoms himself to these habits is no longer master of himself to do the opposite when he wishes, for his will has already become bound in the prison of habit, which becomes a second nature.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:4: Indeed, a person needs to know that he is not in this world for rest, but for labor and toil. He should conduct himself in the manner of laborers who work for their employers, in the vein of what was said (Eruvin 65b): "We are day-laborers" — and in the manner of soldiers going out in their ranks, whose eating is hurried and whose sleep is fleeting, and who stand always ready for the time of battle.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:5: And of this it is said (Job 5:7): "For man is born for toil." And when he accustoms himself to this way, he will certainly find the service light for him, since he will not lack readiness and preparation for it. In this vein our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot 6:4): "Such is the way of Torah: bread with salt shall you eat, water by measure shall you drink, and you shall sleep upon the ground" — this is the general principle of the utmost distancing from comforts and pleasures.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:6: Another thing that undermines alacrity is excessive fear and great dread of the seasons and their consequences: sometimes he fears the cold or the heat, sometimes mishaps, sometimes illnesses, sometimes the wind, and so on with all similar things. This is the matter of which Solomon, peace be upon him, spoke (Proverbs 26:13): "The lazy man says, There is a lion in the road, a lion in the streets."
Mesillat Yesharim 9:7: And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already condemned this trait and attributed it to sinners, and a verse supports them, as it is written (Isaiah 33:14): "The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the hypocrites" — to the point that one of the great sages said to his student, upon seeing him fearful: You are a sinner (Berachot 60a).
Mesillat Yesharim 9:8: Rather, of this it is said (Psalms 37:3): "Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness."
Mesillat Yesharim 9:9: In sum: a person should regard himself as a temporary sojourner in the world and as one firmly established in his service; he should be content and satisfied with whatever presents itself to him in worldly matters, taking what comes into his hand; he should be far from rest and close to labor and toil; his heart should be steadfast, trusting in the Lord, and he should not fear the vicissitudes and mishaps of the season.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:10: Should you say: but we find that the Sages obligated, in every place, that a person guard himself with the utmost care and not place himself in danger, even if he is righteous and a man of good deeds, and they said (Ketubot 30a), "Everything is in the hands of Heaven except colds and chills," and Scripture writes (Deuteronomy 4:15), "and guard yourselves very carefully for your souls" — behold, then, that this trust cannot be relied upon in every case; and there they said, even for a matter of a commandment.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:11: Know that there is fear and there is fear: there is proper fear and there is foolish fear; there is trust and there is recklessness.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:12: For the Master, blessed be He, made man a being of sound intellect and correct judgment, so that he might conduct himself in the way of goodness and guard himself from the harmful things that were created to punish the wicked.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:13: And whoever wishes not to conduct himself in the way of wisdom, and instead abandons himself recklessly to dangers — this is not trust, but recklessness. And indeed he sins in that he acts against the will of the Creator, blessed be His Name, who desires that a person guard himself.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:14: It follows that, besides the danger inherent in the matter to which he is exposed because of his lack of care, he further incurs guilt for his soul through the active sin that he commits, so that the sin itself brings punishment upon him.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:15: However, this care, and this fear founded upon the guidance of wisdom and reason, is the proper one, concerning which it is said (Proverbs 22:3): "The prudent man sees evil and hides himself, but the simple pass on and are punished."
Mesillat Yesharim 9:16: But foolish fear is when a person wishes to keep adding precaution upon precaution and fear upon fear, making a safeguard for his safeguard, in such a way that this results in the neglect of Torah and service.
Mesillat Yesharim 9:17: And the rule for distinguishing between the two fears is what the Sages, of blessed memory, differentiated when they said (Pesachim 8b): "Where danger is common, it is different."
